text: Cash received from café customers for coffee sold, $12 million
explanation: Cash from selling the company's main products is the core of operating activities.

text: Cash paid to coffee-bean suppliers, $5 million
explanation: Paying suppliers for inventory is part of the main trading activity: operating.

text: Salaries paid to baristas, $3 million
explanation: Paying employees who run the cafés is an operating cash outflow.

text: Electricity bills paid for the roastery, $0.4 million
explanation: Day-to-day running costs of the business are operating cash outflows.

text: Cash paid for a new roasting machine, $4 million
explanation: Buying property, plant and equipment (a long-term asset) is an investing cash outflow.

text: Cash received from selling an old delivery van, $0.2 million
explanation: Selling property, plant and equipment is an investing cash inflow.

text: Shares of another company bought as a long-term investment, $2 million
explanation: Buying long-term investments in other entities is an investing activity.

text: Cash received from a fresh issue of equity shares, $10 million
explanation: Raising money from shareholders changes shareholders' funds: financing.

text: Five-year bank loan received, $6 million
explanation: Raising borrowings changes the company's debt: financing.

text: Repayment of a bank loan, $1.5 million
explanation: Repaying borrowings is a financing cash outflow.

text: Interest paid on the bank loan, $0.6 million
explanation: Ind AS 7 (para 33): for a company that is not a financial institution, interest paid is a financing activity.

text: Interest received on fixed deposits, $0.1 million
explanation: Ind AS 7 (para 33): for a company that is not a financial institution, interest received is an investing activity.

text: Dividend received on shares held as an investment, $0.2 million
explanation: Ind AS 7 (para 33): for a company that is not a financial institution, dividends received are an investing activity.

text: Dividend paid to Copperleaf's shareholders, $1 million
explanation: Ind AS 7 (para 34): dividends paid are a financing activity, a return to the providers of equity.

text: Cash paid to buy back Copperleaf's own equity shares, $2 million
explanation: A buyback returns cash to shareholders and reduces shareholders' funds: financing (Ind AS 7, para 17).

text: Income tax paid for the year, $1.2 million
explanation: Ind AS 7 (para 35): income tax paid is an operating activity unless it can be specifically linked to investing or financing. Here it cannot.

text: Cash paid to build a new café (capital work-in-progress), $3 million
explanation: Spending on a long-term asset under construction is purchase of property, plant and equipment: investing.

text: Cash put into a three-year fixed deposit with a bank, $1 million
explanation: A deposit for more than three months is not a cash equivalent, so placing it is an investing activity.

text: Advance received from a customer for a bulk coffee order, $0.5 million
explanation: Cash received from customers for the company's products, even in advance, is an operating inflow.

text: Cash received from selling a long-term investment in shares, $1.5 million
explanation: Selling investments in other entities is an investing cash inflow.

text: Depreciation on roasting machines
explanation: Depreciation reduced profit but used no cash, so it is added back.

text: Amortisation of café software
explanation: Amortisation is a non-cash expense, so it is added back.

text: Increase in trade receivables
explanation: More sales are still unpaid, so less cash came in than the profit shows: deduct the increase.

text: Decrease in trade receivables
explanation: Customers paid off old dues, so more cash came in than the profit shows: add the decrease.

text: Increase in inventory of coffee beans
explanation: Cash was spent on extra stock that is not yet an expense: deduct the increase.

text: Decrease in inventory of coffee beans
explanation: Stock used up was paid for earlier, so the expense used no cash this year: add the decrease.

text: Increase in trade payables
explanation: Suppliers are not yet paid for some purchases, so cash stayed in the company: add the increase.

text: Decrease in trade payables
explanation: Cash was used to pay off old supplier dues: deduct the decrease.

text: Profit on sale of an old delivery van
explanation: The sale proceeds are shown under investing, so the profit is removed from operating: deduct it.

text: Loss on sale of old café equipment
explanation: The loss is not an operating cash outflow (the sale is investing), so it is added back.

text: Finance costs (interest expense) charged in profit and loss
explanation: Under Ind AS 7, interest paid is shown under financing, so the expense is added back to profit before tax.

text: Interest income on fixed deposits
explanation: Under Ind AS 7, interest received is shown under investing, so the income is deducted from profit before tax.
